meta.what_this_is: A measurement of how often a versioned third-party mirror of NFL game results revises records for games that were ALREADY FINAL, using genuine immutable upstream Git vintages. Every vintage is re-downloadable from the recorded codeload URL and identified by SHA-256.
meta.what_it_is_not: Not a count of NFL/Elias corrections, not an official-record statement, and not exhaustive: vintages are sampled at a stride, so a change made and reverted inside one interval is invisible. The mirror is not the NFL.
meta.detector_under_test: pipeline/detect.py diff_final_records() over FROZEN_FIELDS_GAMES, the same code path the scheduled alerting workflow runs.

source.provenance: third-party mirror of NFL schedule/results/lines; not an NFL publication

sampling.note: Sampled intervals are a blind spot by construction: a change made and reverted inside one interval cannot be observed. Reduce --stride to shrink it.

interpretation: Across 44 sampled intervals spanning 1420.67 hours of upstream history, 44 intervals changed the mirrored file's bytes. On games that were ALREADY FINAL, 179 non-scoreboard field change(s) were observed across 91 games (145 late backfills of a blank cell, 34 revisions of an already-published value), and 0 frozen scoreboard-field change(s). The mirror therefore does edit finished games after the fact; in this window none of those edits touched a score, margin, total or overtime flag. Bounded observation about a third-party mirror, not a statement about NFL records.
